verdict.rationale: uv's docs describe `uv.lock` as a cross-platform lockfile holding exact dependency information. `--upgrade-package` updates one package while keeping the rest of the lockfile intact, which suggests minimal, diff-friendly changes. However, the evidence never states the file is plain text or human-readable, and no format specification is cited. The community note that uv once lacked a platform-agnostic lockfile describes the launch state and does not contradict the current docs. missing for 10: explicit evidence that uv.lock is a text-based (e.g. TOML) format, documented lockfile schema/format reference, independent or hands-on corroboration of agents reading/diffing it

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can point an agent at a documented, text-based lockfile format it can read and diff

citations.quote: `uv.lock` is a cross-platform lockfile that contains exact information about your project's dependencies.
The `--upgrade-package` flag will attempt to update the specified package to the latest compatible version, while keeping the rest of the lockfile intact.
This will also update the lockfile and project environment
